payload.claim: The docstring for `_spec_finding_field` says an untyped SQLite column keeps only `None`, `str` and in-range `int` 'without coercion', implying a `float` would be coerced if stored directly and that is why it is `json.dumps`-ed. SQLite's own affinity rule for an untyped (BLOB-affinity) column is 'no attempt is made to coerce data from one storage class into another' for any value, floats included, which is exactly what the correct comment on the table two lines above (saffron/ledger.py:284, 'SQLite's own affinity never rewrites a value (measured)') already says. The two comments describing the same untyped-column mechanism contradict each other: one claims universal no-coercion, the other claims float/bool/list/dict would be coerced. The real reasons `float`, `bool`, `list` and `dict` are special-cased (fact/row round-trip consistency, the sqlite3 bool-to-int adapter, and that lists/dicts cannot bind at all) have nothing to do with column-affinity coercion, so citing 'coercion' here misstates the measured mechanism this codebase otherwise documents precisely.
